"'The Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019' was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 11th December 2019. It is a landmark bill which provides for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognizes both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process personal data for lawful purposes. This is the first Act of the Parliament of India where "she/her" pronouns were used unlike the usual "he/him" pronouns.

Timeline

On 18 November 2022, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology announced the draft of the Data Protection Bill which seeks to provide for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognizes both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process personal data for lawful purposes, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto”.

The bill draws inspiration from the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and is aimed at strengthening the data protection framework in India. It applies to the processing of personal data by both government and private entities, and provides for the establishment of a Data Protection Authority (DPA) to enforce the provisions of the bill.

The bill also introduces the concept of "data fiduciary" and "data principal", where the data fiduciary is the entity that determines the purpose and means of processing personal data, and the data principal is the natural person to whom the personal data relates.

The bill also lays down certain rights for the data principal, such as the right to confirmation and access, the right to correction, the right to data portability, and the right to be forgotten. It also imposes certain obligations on the data fiduciary, such as the obligation to obtain the consent of the data principal, the obligation to provide notice, and the obligation to implement appropriate security safeguards.

The bill also provides for the transfer of personal data outside India, and lays down conditions for such transfer. It also provides for the establishment of a Data Protection Fund to support the implementation of the bill.
